__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: The Prometheus that scrapes brisvox-server's /metrics endpoint

description: brisvox-server: calls and admission, latency per stage, inference pool and Smart Turn pressure, provider failures and usage, from its /metrics endpoint.

panels.title: Calls live
panels.description: Calls running now across the selected instances, with the trend over the time range. Compare with the admission limit in the graph below.

panels.title: Calls refused in range
panels.description: Calls the server refused over the selected time range (at the session limit, under inference pool pressure, at a provider's concurrency budget, or while draining). Every refused call is a caller who did not get through: any value above zero is bad.

panels.title: Response latency p95
panels.description: 95th percentile of the server-side voice-to-voice latency (end of the caller's speech to the first bot audio leaving the engine) over the last rate interval. The network and the client's buffering come on top. Green below 1.0 s, orange to 1.2 s, red above the 1.2 s latency objective used in the benchmarks.

panels.title: Inference pool pressure
panels.description: Whether the server is refusing new calls because the inference pool is behind (queue depth or queue wait over the limits in the operations guide). Normal means the pool is calm. A server that is full or at a provider budget is not shown here: see the refused calls graph.

panels.title: Calls live, % of the session limit
panels.description: Calls running (active) and slots reserved for calls about to start, as a percentage of the BRISVOX_MAX_SESSIONS limit (the absolute count is in the Calls live tile). The server refuses new calls at 100%, and earlier when the inference pool is under pressure. Staying above the dashed 80% line is bad: there is little room for a burst.

panels.title: Calls ended per second, by reason
panels.description: How calls end: completed ran to its end, cancelled was told to stop (per call or by a shutdown), aborted was dropped at the last shutdown stage, failed returned an error, panicked is a bug in the server (that one call died, the others were not affected). Failed, panicked and aborted are bad.

panels.title: Calls refused per second, by reason
panels.description: Why callers were turned away: full is the session limit, overloaded is inference pool pressure, provider_budget is a provider's concurrency limit, shutting_down is a draining server. Any value above zero is bad; the reason says where to look (next sections).

panels.title: Response latency (voice-to-voice, server side)
panels.description: Time from the end of the caller's speech to the first bot audio leaving the engine, p50 and p95. Network and client buffering are not included. The red line is the 1.2 s latency objective used in the benchmarks; a p95 above it is bad.

defaults.noValue: No finished turns in this range

panels.title: Time to silence after a barge-in
panels.description: Time from the accepted barge-in to the engine stopping the bot's audio (the playout is flushed); audio already buffered on the client is not included. Normally tens of milliseconds. A rising p95 means the output stage is slow to clear: interrupted speech is still playing.

panels.title: Stage latency p50
panels.description: Median of each stage of a turn: end_of_turn (the wait before the turn is judged over), stt_final (speech end to the final transcript), llm_first_token (LLM request to its first token), tts_first_byte (TTS request to its first audio). The stages overlap in time, so do not add them up; the biggest one is where the time goes.

defaults.noValue: No finished turns in this range

panels.title: Stage latency p95
panels.description: 95th percentile of the same stages as the graph on the left. A stage whose p95 grows while its p50 stays flat has a slow tail (usually one provider or one region).

defaults.noValue: No finished turns in this range

panels.title: Engine overhead p95 (into the LLM, out of the TTS)
panels.description: The engine's own hops: from the end-of-turn decision to the LLM request (budget 3 ms) and from the first TTS audio to the first audio out (budget 2 ms). Buckets start at 1 ms, so a flat line below 1 ms means "under 1 ms". Growth here means the server is short of CPU, not that a provider is slow.

defaults.noValue: No finished turns in this range

panels.title: Turns interrupted by the caller
panels.description: Share of finished turns that ended in a barge-in (the caller spoke over the bot), over the last rate interval. There is no good value: it depends on the agent and the callers. Watch for a step change: a drop to zero while callers talk over the bot means interruptions stopped working; a sustained rise means the bot is cut off more often than before.

defaults.noValue: No finished turns in this range

panels.title: Barge-in failures per second
panels.description: Clear failures: the transport did not accept or confirm the command that flushes the caller's playback, so the caller may keep hearing the interrupted response. Mark timeouts: the client never echoed the end-of-response mark, so the server ended the response without a playback confirmation. Both are counted when a call ends, so a rate lags the failure by up to a call's length. Any value above zero is bad: check the transport and the client.

panels.title: Why is it slow or refusing?
Inference pool queue depth
panels.description: Jobs (VAD windows, other inference) waiting for a pool thread, sampled at scrape time. The server turns overloaded and refuses calls when the queue holds BRISVOX_OVERLOAD_QUEUE_PER_THREAD (default 4) jobs per pool thread, so the limit depends on the thread count and has no fixed line here; the Inference pool pressure panel shows when it is crossed. Sustained values above zero are bad.

defaults.noValue: No pool metrics: the server hosts no calls

panels.title: Inference pool mean queue wait
panels.description: Mean time jobs waited in the pool queue over the last full window of jobs; it stays at its last value when there are no jobs, so a flat line after traffic stops is not a problem. The red line is 50 ms, the default BRISVOX_OVERLOAD_QUEUE_WAIT: at or above it the server refuses new calls. Waits near the line are bad; they delay VAD and end-of-turn decisions of every call.

defaults.noValue: No pool metrics: the server hosts no calls

panels.title: Provider concurrency in use and limit
panels.description: Calls holding a permit of each provider (solid) against its BRISVOX_PROVIDER_LIMITS limit (dashed), summed over the instances. A provider at its limit refuses new calls (provider_budget). Empty when no limits are set.

panels.title: Smart Turn executor queue depth
panels.description: Smart Turn analyses (the end-of-turn model) waiting for an executor thread. They run on their own threads, so this is invisible in the inference pool graphs. Sustained values above zero mean turns end late. Empty with BRISVOX_SMART_TURN_THREADS=0.

defaults.noValue: Smart Turn executor off or idle

panels.title: Smart Turn analyses lost per second
panels.description: Analyses refused because the executor queue was full (rejected) or answered too late (timed out). Each one makes its turn end at the fallback silence deadline instead of the model's verdict. Any value above zero is bad: add BRISVOX_SMART_TURN_THREADS or shed calls.

defaults.noValue: Smart Turn executor off or idle

panels.title: Circuit breaker state per provider
panels.description: State of each provider's circuit breaker: closed is healthy, half-open is probing after a failure, open means calls to that provider are refused (a secondary takes over if one is configured). Open for more than a minute means the provider is down.

panels.title: Failed provider attempts per second
panels.description: Attempts the circuit breaker counted as failed, per provider and role (a connect, a request or a mid-call session that failed). A provider with a steady rate here is the one to look at.

targets.expr: sum by (stage, role, provider) (rate(brisvox_breaker_events_total{instance=~"$instance", provider=~"$provider", event="failures"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Provider errors per second, by stage and kind
panels.description: Failures the engine counted at the end of calls, by stage and kind (connect failure, session death, LLM request or stream error, first-token or idle timeout, TTS send failure or stall). The counters carry no provider label: use the breaker graph to find the provider.

panels.title: Retries and failovers per second
panels.description: Retries are attempts repeated after a failure; failovers are attempts served by the secondary provider. Both mean a call was saved but a primary is degraded; a steady failover rate means calls run on the secondary.

panels.title: Failures the resilience layer could not absorb
panels.description: unavailable: every provider leg was refused by its breaker; budget_refusals: a retry was denied because the process retry budget was spent (the outage is bigger than the budget); recovery_failures: a mid-call failure that could not be recovered and reached the caller. Any value above zero is bad.

panels.title: LLM tokens in the last hour, by provider, model and kind
panels.description: Tokens the LLM provider reported for finished calls over a rolling hour, including discarded speculative responses. cached_input is part of input: do not add them. Multiply by your price list. A lower bound: a response cancelled mid-way reports no usage.

panels.title: Call duration
panels.description: Duration of finished calls: median, 95th percentile and mean. Call length multiplies every per-minute cost (STT audio, telephony). Buckets run from 5 s to 1 h, so values above 1 h are shown as 1 h.

panels.title: STT audio sent in the last hour
panels.description: Minutes of audio sent to the STT provider by finished calls over a rolling hour, silence included: what a provider that bills by audio time bills for, up to its own rounding. Multiply by your price per audio minute.

panels.title: TTS characters sent in the last hour
panels.description: Characters of text sent to the TTS provider by finished calls over a rolling hour (text replaced by a pre-rendered clip is not counted). Multiply by your price per million characters.

title: Brisvox server
